positions.name: TelephoneCompanyNetworkMoat
positions.frame: How does structural positioning between communicating counterparties create non-commodifiable defensibility against platform incumbents?
positions.why: Xavier argues that software capabilities commodify rapidly unless a company sits in between communicating counterparties ('the telephone company always wins'), creating bilateral network effects where the system is valuable across organizational boundaries. Tanya explores whether federated conversation graphs and cross-company clarification workflows achieve this intermediary defensibility.

positions.name: ReadTimeEpistemicResolution
positions.frame: How should knowledge graph architecture balance append-only conversation provenance with read-time entity and authority resolution?
positions.why: Tanya outlines the V2 ontology architecture: the graph witnesses and preserves raw statements, provenance, and digest narrations without pre-encoding analytical truth or entity disambiguation, leaving authority weighting and entity resolution to generation/read time by the LLM.

positions.name: FundraisingMarketplaceProcessStaging
positions.frame: How should early-stage founders stage advisor introductions and investor conversations to create competitive fundraising momentum?
positions.why: Xavier advises Tanya on fundraising tactics: sequencing advice-seeking before formal raises, holding high-leverage connectors (Emery Park) until a term sheet creates ammunition, running a time-bound process, and framing the raise as creating an open marketplace rather than seeking individual approval.

attaches.why: Tanya articulates the product evolution to organizational perspective graph extraction from transcription services and how the accumulated decision graph functions as the technical moat.
